title: The Way Back to the Eaves
story:
The morning sun slanted across the courtyard tiles, warming the red terra-cotta pots where purple bougainvillea spilled in careless waves. James sat on the low stone coping beside Pippin, testing the hand-painted clay bird whistle Rosa had given him. When he brought it to his lips and blew a tentative puff of air, it produced a clear, two-toned trill—a sweet warble that made Pippin cock his scruffy ears and prompted a quiet laugh from Sofia as she swept the flagstones. It was a bright sound, entirely unlike the deep groans of the town's motor-carriages, lighter even than the chime of clock bells.

He took his leave when the highland breeze began to turn crisp, carrying the familiar faint scent of rain from the distant peaks. He bowed to Rosa with both hands resting lightly against his chest. He touched two fingers to Pippin's warm brow in grateful farewell. He paused at the arched wooden gate just long enough to see Sofia wave her broom in an easy arc of parting. As he stepped out into the winding lane, he chewed the sweet slice of dried potato, savoring the rich, roasted sugar of it until the last crumb was gone.

Oakhaven felt different on the walk back. The cobblestones were no longer an uncharted maze of hard angles; they were paths he had walked before. He passed the quiet lane leading to Mateo's workshop, where the weaver's dyed threads still gleamed braided along his leather strap, and skirted the lower arches of Lookout Bridge where he had once stood in the dawn mist. When he reached the massive carved doors of the Grand Library, he slipped inside with the confident swiftness of one returning to familiar halls, the cool scent of parchment and old ink enveloping him like an old blanket.

High up, at the top of the creaking spiral stairs, the Archive Nook waited beneath the ancient rafters. James climbed into the circular embrasure of his window, untied his strap, and lined up his treasures along the wooden ledge beside his crate: the brass canister, the green sea-glass, the star-shaped seed pod, the spool of deep indigo wool, and the little painted bird whistle. Through the round pane of glass, he watched the afternoon shadows lengthen over the tiled rooftops of Oakhaven. Far below in the square, a flock of pigeons lifted all at once, their wings catching the white glint of the sky before disappearing into the eaves.
location: The Archive Nook, Grand Library, Oakhaven
